sections.reference_shloka:
सर्जकांजिकसंसिद्धं तैलं शीताम्बुमर्दितम्। 
ज्वरदाहापहं लेपात्सद्यो वातास्रदाहनुत्।। (Sahasrayogam) 

 The verse explains that oil processed with Sarjarasa and Kanji alleviates burning sensation in fever and provides relief in Vatarakta when applied externally after mixing with cold water.
sections.composition:
I. Main Ingredients 

 Sarjarasa (Shorea robusta – Sal Tree Resin) – 1 part 
 Murchita Tila Taila (Sesamum indicum – Processed Sesame Oil) – 4 parts 
 Kanji (Fermented Sour Rice Gruel) – 16 parts 

 Method Of Preparation 
 A clean stainless steel vessel is taken and processed sesame oil is poured into it. Sarjarasa, purified and powdered, is added to the oil and mixed thoroughly. The prescribed quantity of Kanji is then incorporated into the mixture. The contents are heated over mild fire following the classical Sneha Paka procedure. Continuous stirring is maintained to ensure uniform processing and to prevent sticking of the resin to the vessel base. The mixture is heated until the aqueous component of Kanji evaporates completely and only medicated sesame oil remains in its original oil quantity. Proper completion is identified by the absence of moisture, characteristic aroma of processed resin, and formation of soft, non-adherent residue. After self-cooling, the oil is filtered through a clean cloth and stored in airtight glass containers. 
 Method Of Use 
 The medicated oil is mixed with cold water and applied locally over the affected area. Application is generally performed as a thin topical layer or gentle external massage as advised by an Ayurvedic practitioner.
sections.pharmacological_actions:
Reduces burning sensation associated with fever 
 Soothes inflamed and heat-affected tissues 
 Provides cooling and calming external effect 
 Supports comfort in conditions involving peripheral heat and irritation 
 Helps pacify aggravated Pitta and Vata in localized tissues 

 Clinical Indications 

 Burning sensation during febrile conditions 
 Vatarakta associated with localized heat and discomfort 
 External support therapy in inflammatory conditions with thermal symptoms. 

 Method Of Administration 
 External application only. The oil should be diluted with cold water before local use as indicated in classical instructions. 
 Commentary 
 The formulation is documented in classical Ayurvedic literature – Chakradatta addressing fever management and conditions characterized by burning sensation. It is specifically described as a topical preparation processed with fermented sour medium and resin, indicating its specialized role in thermal disorders of the body surface.
sections.precautions:
For external use only. Application should be performed under the guidance of a qualified Ayurvedic practitioner. Avoid application on open wounds unless specifically advised. Store in airtight glass containers away from direct heat and sunlight. 
 Conclusion 
 Sarjadi Taila is a classical medicated oil prepared by processing Sal tree resin in sesame oil using fermented sour gruel through the Sneha Paka method. The formulation is primarily indicated for external application in burning sensation associated with fever and Vatarakta. Its cooling and soothing action, especially when applied after dilution with cold water, makes it a supportive topical therapy for localized heat-related discomfort when prepared and used according to classical guidelines.
